e: Nitrogen is the non-metallic element with the symbol N and atomic number 7. Non-metallic element with the symbol and atomic number.

q: A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by ____.
e: A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by three covalent bonds. An N2 molecule holds two nitrogen atoms with a triple covalent bond, which is why nitrogen is so unreactive. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: Nitrogen is a ____ without any smell and is very unreactive.
e: Nitrogen is a colourless gas without any smell and is very unreactive. Nitrogen gas is very unreactive because of the strong triple bond in N2.

q: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of ____.
e: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of -196℃. Nitrogen has a very low boiling point, which is why it is a gas at room temperature and is separated from liquid air.

q: The Earth's atmosphere is made up of ____ of nitrogen, with the rest being oxygen, carbon dioxide and other trace elements.
e: The Earth's atmosphere is made up of 78 percentage of nitrogen, with the rest being oxygen, carbon dioxide and other trace elements. About 78 percent of clean dry air is nitrogen. Clean dry air is about 78 percent nitrogen by volume. The mixture of gases around Earth is the atmosphere, and that mixture exerts pressure.

q: Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by ____ from which carbon dioxide and water have been removed.
e: Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by fractional distillation of liquid air from which carbon dioxide and water have been removed. Fractional distillation of liquid air separates nitrogen, oxygen and argon by boiling point. Industrial nitrogen is taken from liquid air by fractional distillation.

q: Since the nitrogen is only slightly soluble in water, it is collected by the ____.
e: Since the nitrogen is only slightly soluble in water, it is collected by the downward displacement of water. Listen for downward displacement of water in that sentence.

q: The main use of nitrogen is in the manufacture of ____, from which nitrogenous fertilisers, nitric acid and urea are mainly prepared.
e: The main use of nitrogen is in the manufacture of ammonia gas, from which nitrogenous fertilisers, nitric acid and urea are mainly prepared. Ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen and is the feedstock for nitrogen fertiliser. Nitric acid is manufactured from ammonia by catalytic oxidation in the Ostwald process.

q: Since nitrogen has ____ in its outermost shell, the oxidation numbers of nitrogen vary from -3 to +5.
e: Since nitrogen has 5 electrons in its outermost shell, the oxidation numbers of nitrogen vary from -3 to +5. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Nitrogen has five outer electrons, so its oxidation numbers run from -3 to +5. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.
